bullets.title: NVDA: $250B OpenAI data center backstop, $500B SK Group deal, $1.5B Amkor packaging—AI infrastructure dominance
bullets.body: NVDA is in talks to guarantee ~$250B in financing for OpenAI's 10GW Ohio data center (total cost >$500B), and may backstop $350B in chip purchases. Separately, NVDA and SK Group announced a $500B+ AI factory and HBM4 memory co-development initiative (SK Telecom building 2GW Vera Rubin campus), NVDA committed $1B into Naver/Brookfield for Korean AI infrastructure, and NVDA signed a $1.5B multi-year deal with Amkor for U.S. advanced packaging. Multiple brokers also note NVDA expanding its role from chip supplier to financier/credit backer of AI infrastructure, raising ROI debate.

bullets.title: AVGO/Samsung $200B MOU + SK Hynix $750B memory deals reshape AI supply chain
bullets.body: Samsung and Broadcom signed a $200B MOU through 2030 spanning AI accelerators (2nm foundry), HBM, and advanced packaging—with Samsung supplying 75–85% of AVGO's HBM requirements. SK Hynix separately announced $750B in long-term memory partnerships with U.S. tech customers including the $500B+ SK Group/NVIDIA initiative. UBS estimates combined hyperscaler capex framework at $1.34T in 2027E and $1.48T in 2028E (+43%/+11% YoY).

bullets.title: MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN earnings previews: heavy AI capex scrutiny, Azure at 39–40%
bullets.body: MSFT reports Wed 7/29 ($4.24 EPS est); Azure guided to 39–40% growth vs consensus ~41%, with investor target ~43% by Dec '26. UBS cuts MSFT PT to $480 from $510, citing FY27 capex raised to $261B; Ackman calls MSFT at 21x its cheapest valuation in a decade. META faces focus on operating profit revisions; AAPL seen beating on Products/iCloud with Apple Intelligence momentum and outperforming NDX by 22 ppts in July. AMZN 2Q AWS expected at 35–36% post-GOOG read-through.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $200B capex raised, Cloud backlog $514B, upgraded to Buy at Phillip Capital; GOOG FCF turns negative
bullets.body: Alphabet raised 2026 capex guidance by $15B to $195–205B midpoint with '27 capex expected to 'increase significantly.' GCP backlog surged +385% YoY to $514B. GOOGL FCF turned negative (~$5.9B) in 2Q on the massive build-out. Phillip Capital upgraded to Buy with $425 PT (33% upside). JPM notes GOOGL is down ~8% on the week but recommends buying the pullback; Chamath cites 32% 25-year ROIC as compelling compounder.

bullets.title: INTC: Server CPU ASPs +48%, DCAI +59%—strongest results in 15 years, then crashed 17% intraday
bullets.body: INTC delivered strongest revenue growth in 15 years (+25% YoY vs 12% consensus) with DCAI revenue +59% to $6.3B vs $5.4B estimate. Server CPU ASPs jumped 48% per 10-Q. Stock surged +10% after-hours but reversed to close -7% on the day (17% intraday whipsaw). Ohio Senate confirmed Intel-SK Hynix Ohio chip plant partnership. INTC also announced €5B Leixlip Ireland campus expansion for AI/HPC.

bullets.title: VZ: 2Q beat with postpaid phone adds +184K, raised 2026 guidance 2.5–3% growth; AT&T 11% weekly outperformance
bullets.body: Verizon beat on postpaid phone net adds (+184K vs -9K YoY) driven by subsidy-free Simplicity plan; raised 2026 mobility+broadband revenue guidance to 2.5–3%, EPS to $4.99–5.04 (+6–7%), FCF growth to 9–10%, and buyback authorization to $4.5B. Announced $1B+ dark fiber deal with Google. MS raises PT from $50 to $52 but keeps Equal-weight citing better-growing peers. Separately, AT&T launched a five-part Euro/GBP bond offering and outperformed the S&P 500 by 11%+ last week, its largest weekly beat in 25 years, aided by D-Wave quantum computing expansion.

bullets.title: CHTR: Broadband competition accelerating; Citi/UBS cut PT sharply
bullets.body: Charter reported 2Q EBITDA -4.3% YoY with broadband HSD subs -212K; management lowered 2026 EBITDA guidance to -1% decline vs. prior growth expectation. Citi maintains Buy but cuts PT to $180 on 2027 FCF upside as capex recedes. UBS cuts PT sharply to $140 from $235, applying ~5x forward EBITDA with a discount for accelerating competitive intensity from fiber, FWA, and emerging satellite competition.

bullets.title: GLW: Downgraded to Neutral at JPM; optical demand strong but TV display pricing cracking
bullets.body: JPM downgrades GLW to Neutral citing LCD panel prices declining -2.1% m/m in July (vs seasonal +1.4%) with August tracking -2.7%. Multiple brokers (MS, Jefferies) note GLW is 30%+ below mid-cycle peaks on sector unwind, not fundamentals. Optical enterprise revenue expected +28% YoY and CIEN/GLW seen as best plays on AI network buildout but investors unwilling to step in pre-earnings. JPM recommends put spreads on elevated expectations (~9.6% implied move vs. 4.9% avg realized).

bullets.title: SHOP: Beat-and-raise setup; JPM adds to Focus List with $155 PT
bullets.body: JPM projects 2026 SHOP GMV +29% YoY with revenue +30% YoY and FCF margin 18%. Chase Card data shows 2Q U.S. CNP growth +11% YoY, accelerating from 1Q. Earnings implied move ~10.5% vs. 12.8% avg realized—call spreads recommended as entry. GPM bullish on AI adoption across traffic, on-platform, and infrastructure layers.

bullets.title: AAPL: Lobbying for Chinese memory chips outside US; MU opposing; stock +22% vs Nasdaq in July
bullets.body: Apple is aggressively lobbying the White House to permit Chinese memory chips (CXMT, YMTC) in devices sold outside the U.S.; Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra is pushing back. Apple benefiting from asset-light AI strategy and memory price tension has boosted stock to +22% vs NDX in July—largest monthly outperformance in 20 years. Jefferies raises AAPL PT to $308.92.

bullets.title: GEV: Record $24.2B 2Q orders (vs $20.1B est); JPM raises YE27 PT to $1,330
bullets.body: GE Vernova reported 2Q orders of $24.2B beat, signing ~20GW gas power contracts vs. 10–15GW guidance. FCF guidance raised to $11.5–12.5B from $6.5–7.5B; gas capacity now complete at 20GW on track for 30GW by 2030. JPM establishes YE27 PT of $1,330, maintains Overweight; Mizuho raises PT 4% to $949. Goldman favors VST and TLN alongside GEV on power fundamentals.

bullets.title: WBD: Downgraded to Neutral; Paramount agrees to delay merger to mid-2027, heads to trial
bullets.body: Seaport Research downgraded WBD to Neutral. Paramount agreed to delay the $110B WBD merger close until June 2027 (or antitrust resolution) and will pay $650M/quarter until closure. The deal bypasses the preliminary injunction hearing and proceeds directly to trial in California, which LightShed notes may require Paramount to make structural alterations. PSKY is pressed by 12 state AGs and the Writers Guild.

bullets.title: PLTR: Strong 2Q beat expected; >75% growth guide; hospital tool study raises product risk
bullets.body: OPCO maintains Outperform with $200 PT, expecting PLTR to beat 2Q guidance and raise FY guide to >75% growth with US Commercial >135% YoY and Government mid-80s% growth. FT study reports PLTR's hospital discharge optimization tool did not reduce discharge delays in studied institutions, raising questions about product efficacy.

bullets.title: SPOT: AI tier uncertainty; -10% since Investor Day despite UMG deal; Q3 margin headwinds
bullets.body: SPOT faces Q3 gross margin headwind of -30 to -40 bps from a regulatory charge; investors expect at least +20 bps Q2 GM beat to 33.3%. Stock is down 10% since May Investor Day despite margin upgrades and UMG licensing deal. Labels threw cold water on AI tier artist opt-in rates, adding uncertainty. JPM calls it a crowded long.

bullets.title: UBER: Waymo explores exit from partnership; stock hits 52-week lows
bullets.body: FT reports Waymo is exploring options to exit its Uber robotaxi partnerships in Atlanta and Austin, potentially starting Jan 2028. Current Uber-Waymo exclusivity contract runs through ~May 2028. Ackman's Pershing Square holds $1.98B UBER position, calling it a solid franchise. Stock hit new 52-week lows this week.

bullets.title: DDOG: Enters earnings as crowded long; bulls need 5+ point beat at 19.5x FY26 revenue
bullets.body: DDOG rallied +80% YTD into earnings as a crowded long. JPM expects ~$1.125B Q2 revenue (~+36% YoY) vs. Street ~$1.075B. Investors need a 5+ point beat to appease bulls at ~19.5x FY26 revenue. Anthropic tailwinds expected to continue; OpenAI share losses from PANW Chronosphere offsetting. Q2 seasonality: +6% Q/Q beat expected similar to Q4-Q1 pattern.

bullets.title: WSM: Piper Sandler initiates Overweight $253 PT; best-in-class EBIT margin, HSD% sales growth
bullets.body: Piper Sandler initiates WSM at Overweight with $253 PT (25x 2027E EPS, 12% upside). Cites best-in-class EBIT margins with consistent outperformance in depressed home furnishing backdrop. Expects sales growth acceleration to HSD% over 2–3 years driving mid-teens EPS growth; Q2 estimates have upside.

bullets.title: AMD: Mizuho raises PT to $625; CEO Lisa Su visits South Korea; Vultr AI cloud deployment
bullets.body: Mizuho raises AMD PT to $625 from $615. AMD CEO Lisa Su visited South Korea for strategic meetings. Vultr deploys AMD EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs across 33 global regions for its AI public cloud. UBS models AMD C2027E EPS ~$19 with bull case ~$30 in C2028 on DC GPU growth. AMD and Cerebras collaboration on prefill/decode memory splitting noted.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Citi cuts PT to $30, maintains Buy; NBCU spin mid-2027 catalyst; Odyssey box office
bullets.body: Comcast reported mixed 2Q with domestic connectivity improving but slower pace; Citi maintains Buy and cuts PT to $30. NBCU/SKY spin expected mid-2027. Weekend box office $141.5M with CMCSA's The Odyssey leading at $87M domestic ($286M cumulative). NBCU also generated $440M+ incremental revenue from World Cup in 2Q per Supino analysis.

bullets.title: CORZ downgraded to Market Perform at KBW; WULF/CIFR initiated at Buy by Chardan; HOOD exploring prediction market partnerships
bullets.body: KBW downgraded CORZ to Market Perform (from Outperform), cutting PT to $25 from $28 (10% upside). Chardan initiated WULF at Buy with $32 PT (73% upside) and CIFR at Buy with $32 PT (38% upside). Robinhood (HOOD) is in talks with Crypto.com to expand into prediction markets, and is separately exploring crypto partnerships per Bloomberg.
